Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 27626 of 2024

Applicant :- Amit Kumar Verma Alias Jaikky
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Ishan Deo Giri,Krishna Shukla
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Counter affidavit filed today on behalf of the State is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Ishan Deo Giri, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Kunwar Tejendra Bahadur,
learned AGA for the State.
3.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 422 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Kotwali Ballia, District Ballia during pendency of the trial.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and his family members and according to the FIR marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the daughter of the informant on 02.12.2022 and after marriage applicant and his family members tortured her for a car and Rs. 3 lakhs.

It is further mentioned in the FIR that applicant was also having illicit relationship with his Bhabhi and on Amit Kumar Verma Alias Jaikky vs State Of U.P. on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170452419/
1 06.08.2023 informant received an information that applicant and his family members committed the murder of his daughter.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that on the basis of false allegation, applicant has been made accused in the present matter only being husband of the deceased.

6. He further submits that actually deceased i.e. wife of the applicant was having doubt that applicant is having illicit relationship with his Bhabhi, therefore, she committed suicide and this fact has been mentioned by the informant in the FIR itself.
7. He further submits that post mortem report of the deceased suggests that deceased died due to hanging.
He further submits that during trial informant i.e. father of the deceased and her brother appeared before the trial court and brother of the deceased has been declared hostile.

8. He further submits that however father of the deceased did not declare hostile but in cross examination he did not support the prosecution case and stated that on the instigation of other persons he lodged FIR of the present case.

9. He further submits that after considering the statements of both the witnesses i.e. father and brother of the deceased recorded by the trial court, the chances of conviction of applicant are quite remote.
10. He further submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 08.08.2023 i.e. for last a year.

11. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but he could not dispute the fact that when brother of the deceased appeared before the trial court then he did not support the prosecution case and has been declared hostile.
12.

Learned AGA further could not dispute the fact that however father of the deceased i.e.
informant of the case in examination-in-chief supported the prosecution case but in his cross examination he did not support the prosecution case and categorically stated that on the instigation of some persons, he lodged FIR of the present case.
He further could not dispute the fact that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 08.08.2023 i.e. for last a year.
13. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

14. Applicant is however husband of the deceased and his wife died under abnormal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but record suggests that when father of the deceased i.e. informant of the case when appeared before the trial court as PW-1 then however in examination-in-chief he supported the prosecution case but when on Amit Kumar Verma Alias Jaikky vs State Of U.P. on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170452419/

sentences.text: 2 same day his cross examination was recorded then during cross examination he did not support the prosecution case and stated that on the instigation of some other persons, he lodged FIR of the present case and he also stated that his daughter was never harassed for demand of dowry.
15. Record also suggest that after the testimony of the father when brother of the deceased appeared before the trial court then he has been declared hostile.

16. Further, considering the post mortem report of the deceased which shows that deceased died due to hanging and the fact which is also mentioned in the FIR that applicant was having illicit relationship with his Bhabhi, the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that deceased was having suspicion that applicant was having illicit relationship with his Bhabhi,
therefore, she committed suicide, cannot be completely ruled out.
17. Further, applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 08.08.2023 i.e. for last one year.

18. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
19. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

20. Let the applicant - Amit Kumar Verma @ Jaikky be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
21.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

22. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
